summary: Goldman Sachs Oil Comment dated 2026-06-05 estimates April 2026 global oil demand destruction at 4-5 mb/d from the Hormuz shock, using three approaches: refinery runs/product stocks, high-frequency demand plus retail prices, and external forecaster/trading-house estimates.
keyClaims: Goldman estimates 4-5 mb/d global oil demand destruction in April 2026, or 4-5% versus a no-war counterfactual.
Approach 1 using refinery runs and product stocks implies just under 4 mb/d demand destruction after including about a 2 mb/d non-refined demand hit.
Approach 2 using high-frequency demand and retail fuel price changes implies just over 5 mb/d demand destruction.
Approach 3 averages other forecasters and trading houses around 4 mb/d.
Goldman says Brent/WTI 2026Q4 forecast risks around $90/$83 per barrel are two-sided.

summary: S&P Global Energy/Platts whitepaper (May 2026) defining criteria for commercially reopening the Strait of Hormuz. Traffic collapsed 90%+ from 135 vessels/day pre-war to 11 vessels/day by late May. Five-factor framework for reopening: vessel traffic recovery (50-90% of pre-war, 1 week to 1 month), observation period (30-45 days after ceasefire), marine insurance availability, physical security (mine clearance), and fleet deployment patterns (VLCC return).
keyClaims: Pre-war (Feb 2026): ~135 vessels/day, 54 oil/chem/LPG tankers, 6 LNG carriers through Strait
By late May: 11 vessels/day, <2 tankers/day - more than 90% below pre-war
US blockade in Gulf of Oman from mid-April - no Iranian crude tankers confirmed through both Strait and blockade since
Non-tanker vessels (landing craft, tugs, cargo ships) now dominate Strait traffic (>50% in May)
War risk premiums surged 1000%+ from 0.1-0.3% to 2.5-5% of hull value
800+ vessels remain stranded in Middle East Gulf
Five minimum conditions needed for commercial reopening
Market feedback: 50-90% of pre-war traffic threshold, sustained 1 week to 1 month
Market feedback: 30-45 day observation period after ceasefire
Short-lived "open" windows (<24h post-ceasefire, ~48h US corridor) immediately reversed, creating credibility gap

summary: Macquarie desk strategy (23 Mar 2026): Strait of Hormuz SOH normally transits ~15 M BPD crude + ~5 M BPD products. Post-conflict: ~1.5 M BPD transiting, leaving 13.5 M BPD deficit. Six mitigation sources analyzed with maximum/expected values. Price floor 5-90 Brent, drift to 10. If shut until end-April, Brent could reach 50, products 200%+ higher. Base case ceasefire end-Mar, Long War ceasefire end-Apr. Asia refinery run cuts could reach 3.5 M BPD max.
keyClaims: SOH normally ~15 M BPD crude + ~5 M BPD products = ~20% of global supply

~11 M BPD production could be shut-in by end of March (~13% of global)
